title: Tobogganing rules and winter parks risk program
subtitle: Also: home energy retrofit loans, heritage notices, plow truck, road stabilization, trail grant, theatre report, façade grants.
overview: Council set a path for tobogganing after safety concerns led to no-tobogganing signs earlier this winter. For the rest of the season, tobogganing is allowed at Foote Park and Southridge Park, and temporarily prohibited on the high-risk part of Ferrier Park {{vote:m15}}. Staff will build a formal winter activities risk management program, covering tobogganing and community ice rinks, and report back by June {{vote:m13}}. Council also approved extra staffing for it {{vote:m14}}.

Council backed the County's Home Energy Efficiency Transition Program and asked staff to prepare a Local Improvement Charge by-law {{vote:m6}}. It adopted a policy to publish Ontario Heritage Act notices on the Township website {{vote:m7}}. It approved a $373,383 plow truck purchase with a $13,383 reserve top-up {{vote:m8}}, and a $203,520 road base stabilization contract for Second Line {{vote:m9}}.

Council directed an Active Transportation Fund application for Elora-Cataract Trail improvements in Fergus {{vote:m10}}. It sent the Fergus Grand Theatre report out for public and committee feedback {{vote:m11}}. It also authorized the 2025 Community Improvement Program incentives, including façade grants {{vote:m12}}. A fees and charges item was deferred, and the minutes report nothing from closed session. Two public meetings on rural severance rezonings drew no questions.

decisions.detail: Tobogganing is permitted at Foote Park and Southridge Park for the rest of the winter with interim risk practices, and temporarily prohibited on the high-risk areas of Ferrier Park until a final report.
Council approved the additional staffing needed for the Winter Activities Risk Management Program, as outlined in report CS2025-10.
Council supports the program, directed staff to prepare a Local Improvement Charge by-law, and authorized the Mayor to send a letter of support for the County's FCM grant application.
Council adopted a policy allowing Ontario Heritage Act notices to be published on the Township website instead of in a newspaper.
Council awarded the purchase to Viking Cives at an upset limit of $373,383 and approved $13,383 more from the General Capital Reserve.
Council approved a single-source contract with BioDiffusion Technologies Inc. at an upset limit of $203,520 for bio-resin road base stabilization.
Staff will apply for federal funding for Elora-Cataract Trail improvements on a new alignment through Fergus, and will report back on the Township's share of the cost if the application succeeds.
Council received the report, sent it for public feedback on ConnectCW and to three advisory committees, and approved the pre-approvals in report CS2025-04.

debate: On the energy retrofit program, one councillor asked how people who cannot afford a loan, or want only one project, would be served. County staff said consumer protections would screen out those unable to repay. Loans have a $10,000 minimum, and incentives for lower-income households are being sought.

On heritage notices, one councillor worried that seniors who rely on the newspaper would miss notices. Staff said owners will still be notified directly and appeal rights are unchanged. Staff also said a newspaper ad would announce the change. Notices of intent are about a page long, so batching would not reduce cost.

On the plow truck, one councillor asked why the price gap was not known at budget time. Staff cited rising heavy truck costs, the weaker Canadian dollar, and model-year pricing that is not known until mid-year.

On tobogganing, councillors stressed equitable access to hills and opposed an outright ban. Staff said the Ferrier Park slope has trees, benches, concrete blocks and little run-out, and warned it may not be possible to make that area safe.

On staffing, some councillors asked about deferring approval until the June report or sharing the role with summer work. Staff said there was no consequence to waiting but that the added service level would still need staff. Supporters said one parks coordinator cannot cover winter duties, and staff will look at a shared position in the 2026 staffing strategy.
